title: Best Carbon Monoxide Alarms UK
short: Six carbon monoxide alarms tested with an aerosol trigger spray in a sealed bag to check response speed, from a £17 basic alarm to a £109 smart detector.
intro: Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless, so a genuinely responsive alarm is one of the few home safety products where a slow reaction can be life-threatening. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (published 14 May 2024), where testers sprayed a specific aerosol test spray for up to three seconds into a transparent plastic bag containing each alarm, checking whether the response was instant, and rejecting any alarm that wasn't. They also assessed controls, displays, any Wi-Fi or app features, and how easy each alarm was to fit using its supplied fittings and instructions.

products.name: Nest Protect
products.badge: Best smart CO and smoke detector

products.summary: Expert Reviews rated this the most aesthetically pleasing option on test, with smartphone notifications, combined smoke detection and informative alerts that tell you what's wrong and where, rather than just sounding an alarm. It also includes emergency pathway lighting to help you find an exit.

guide.q: How does the aerosol test actually work?
guide.a: Expert Reviews sprayed a specific aerosol test spray for up to three seconds into a sealed transparent bag containing each alarm, checking whether the response was instant. Any alarm that didn't respond instantly wasn't recommended, so every alarm in this guide passed that basic but crucial functional test.

guide.q: Do I need a smart, app-connected alarm?
guide.a: A smart alarm like the Nest Protect or Netatmo Smart CO Alarm sends notifications to your phone even when you're not home, useful for holiday homes or checking on elderly relatives remotely. A basic alarm like the Kidde Lifesaver 5CO is cheaper and just as effective at sounding a loud local alarm, which is all that's needed if someone is always home to hear it.

guide.q: Combined smoke and CO alarm, or separate units?
guide.a: A combined alarm like the X-Sense SC-08 or Nest Protect saves fitting two separate devices and reduces the number of things to maintain. Separate dedicated alarms can be positioned more precisely for each hazard, since CO alarms should go near fuel-burning appliances while smoke alarms suit hallways and landings.

guide.q: How long do these alarms actually last?
guide.a: All six alarms in this guide have a 10-year overall lifespan, standard for modern CO alarms, though battery replacement intervals vary: some use replaceable AA batteries needing changes every 2-3 years, while others use a sealed lithium battery that lasts the alarm's full life but can't be swapped if it fails early.
